package.title: Runtimeは同じ月に何を吸収したか — Transformers v5・vLLM・SGLang
package.editorial_angle: Transformers v5の共通実装刷新とvLLM/SGLangのserving evolutionを通じ、モデル・tool API・diffusion・long-context changesがruntimeへどれだけ速く流れ込んだかを見る。

claims.text: Hugging Face released Transformers v5 on January 26, its first major release in five years, with significant API changes including a new dynamic weight-loading/WeightConverter design and tokenizer changes.
The v5 release notes describe breaking changes and quantization/loading cleanup, including migration away from deprecated loading paths and broader architectural refactoring.
The v5.0.0rc3 notes added GLM-4.7/GLM-Image support and MiniMax-M2 support shortly before the stable release, illustrating rapid integration of contemporary model families.

limitations.text: The RC and stable release occurred on the same date; stable v5 is the primary event and rc3 is supporting model-integration evidence.
Library support indicates implementation compatibility, not endorsement or independently measured model quality.

claims.text: vLLM v0.14.0 enabled async scheduling by default and added numerous engine, tool-calling, API, and model-support changes; the release notes explicitly call this a breaking change with unsupported configurations documented.
vLLM v0.15.0 added a Kimi-K2.5 architecture among new model support and extended async scheduling to pipeline parallelism, alongside streaming-input, quantization, and platform changes.
Any speedup figures in the release notes are project-reported and configuration dependent.

limitations.text: The series spans two releases nine days apart and should be summarized as serving/runtime evolution rather than one atomic feature.
Project performance claims are not independently reproduced.

claims.text: SGLang v0.5.8 added day-zero GLM-4.7-Flash support, expanded diffusion serving, FlashAttention 4 decoding support, and multiple long-context / disaggregated-serving changes.
Release-note performance figures such as up to 1.5x diffusion speedups, near-linear chunked-pipeline scaling, and a 65% TTFT improvement for a GLM4-MoE setup are project-reported claims.

limitations.text: The release aggregates many upstream PRs and performance claims across different models/hardware.
Model support establishes implementation availability, not equivalent quality or production validation.
